context_excerpt: 2025-02-16 **Event**: Eleven judges of Country Y Institution J2 held a hearing in City C on February 16, pressing government lawyers over the legality of President Leader A's broad tariffs. The court is composed of 8 judges appointed by Party B presidents and 3 appointed by Party A presidents. The case stems from a lawsuit brought against Leader A by Company B2, challenging his power to unilaterally impose tariffs un…

time.desc: The ruling team A announced the implementation of a package of punitive tariffs on multiple trading partners, covering steel, aluminum, automobiles, agricultural products and other fields.
Institution U Keeps benchmark interest rate unchanged due to economic uncertainty caused by tariffs
Country Q Officials publicly respond and criticize Country Y’s tariff threats for the first time

For the first time, the foreign affairs department of an energy-importing country has publicly criticized the sponsoring country's tariff threat as "unfair and unreasonable" and countered that the other country is still trading with the conflicting party.
The ruling team A announced the imposition of high tariffs on imported semiconductors and the establishment of exemption clauses for local factory construction.
Country Y further increases tariffs on Country Q citing purchases of Country P oil

The sponsoring country officially announced the imposition of extremely high tariffs on semiconductors and the establishment of an exemption for local factory construction and a recovery mechanism for unfulfilled duties.

The initiating country formally imposed an additional 2.5% tariff on an energy importing country, raising the total tax rate to 50%, on the grounds that it purchased oil from conflict parties. The country responded by calling the move 'unfair, unreasonable, and without justifiable reasons.'

The authorities of a technology-producing area submitted formal opinions to the sponsoring country on semiconductor tariffs and sought exemptions, warning that tax increases would increase business costs and reduce investment willingness.
Region T Authorities submit comments to Country Y on semiconductor tariffs and seek exemptions
Country Y The additional tariffs imposed on Region T products have officially come into effect, affecting many types of products.

The 20% tariff imposed by the sponsoring country on goods from a certain technological origin has officially come into effect, affecting the export of machine tools, plastic products, orchids, seafood and other agricultural products.
Many Region E central banks cut interest rates to defend against the impact of the trade war, and a regional monetary easing trend formed
Many regional central banks unexpectedly cut interest rates to defend against the impact of the trade war, and a trend of regional monetary easing is taking shape.
Country W The President publicly stated that he is considering imposing additional tariffs on countries that have not signed free trade agreements.

For the first time, a head of state from a neighboring country publicly announced that he is studying to impose tariffs on imported goods that have not signed a free trade agreement to cope with the pressure of the trade war and prevent his country from becoming a transit point.
Country Y Top judicial body approves expedited trial of President's broad power to impose tariffs, tariffs upheld during trial

The highest judicial body of the sponsoring country approved a fast-track trial on the president’s broad power to impose tariffs and arranged subsequent court sessions, during which the tariffs were maintained
Country Y The President called on third-party organizations to impose high tariffs on Country X and Country Q to pressure Country P

During a meeting with officials from a regional group, the leader of the sponsoring country called on the group to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the two main buyers of oil from the conflict parties to put pressure on ending a certain conflict.
Country Y and Country X hold new round of talks to extend temporary trade truce
The President shall make decisions on the enforcement or postponement of laws requiring the separation of Product D from its parent company

The two major economies held a new round (the fourth round) of negotiations to extend the temporary tariff truce. The topics covered national security, economy and trade, the divestment of a certain short video application and cooperation in combating money laundering networks.
Trade Agency A officially launches Agreement A review process and opens public consultation
The trade authority of the sponsoring country officially launched the review process of a regional comprehensive trade agreement and opened public consultation
President announces plans to use tariff revenue to provide cash assistance to distressed farmers
Country X refuses to budge in soybean purchase talks and blames Country Y tariffs for woes

The leaders of the sponsoring countries announced that they plan to use tariff revenue to provide cash assistance to distressed farmers. The plan must be approved by the legislative body and the funds are expected to be available early next year.
In soybean purchase negotiations, rival economies have made it clear that they will not give in and blame the sponsoring country's tariff policies for the plight of their own soybean farmers.
Country Y calls for an app that reminds immigrants to avoid law enforcement to be removed from the app store
The judicial director of the sponsoring country requested the removal of a crowdsourcing app that reminded users to avoid immigration law enforcement. The platform removed it due to security risks.
The President threatens to impose approximately 100% tariffs on Country X goods and hints at restricting exports of aircraft parts

The leader of the sponsoring country publicly threatened to impose 100% tariffs on goods from a major economy in a few months and hinted at restricting the export of aircraft parts, which may end the fragile trade truce.
The President officially announced the imposition of 100% tariffs on Country X imported goods and plans to control the export of key software
Country X refuses to back down from tariff threat and counters with port charges on Country Y ships

The sponsoring country officially announced that it would impose a 100% tariff on imported goods from a major economy on the basis of the existing tax rate on the grounds that the other party has implemented new export controls.

The diplomatic authorities of rival economies stated that they would not back down from the threat of tariffs and announced countermeasures to impose port fees on ships associated with the sponsoring country.
Rival economies have officially begun to levy port fees on ships associated with the sponsoring country, which will be charged based on net tonnage and will increase year by year.
The sponsoring country imposes new tariffs on imported lumber, cabinets and upholstered furniture, most of which come from rival economies.

Rival economies have expressed in tough terms that they are not afraid of war and are open to negotiations, pointing out that the other side cannot demand dialogue while imposing new restrictions and threats.

The trade and finance chiefs of the sponsoring countries made a joint appearance for the first time, characterizing the rare earth export restrictions of rival economies as 'economic coercion' and threatening that the world will have to decouple from them.

Leaders of the sponsoring countries signed an executive order to impose a 25% tariff on imported medium- and heavy-duty trucks, with partial exemptions for regional agreements, and a lower tax rate for passenger cars.

The leader of the sponsoring country announced the termination of all trade negotiations with a neighboring country because the local government of the neighboring country placed an advertisement that quoted the former president's criticism of tariffs.

The neighboring country's regional government responded by saying it would pause advertising in the sponsoring country to allow negotiations to resume, but ads would continue to air during major weekend events.

The financial and economic chief of the sponsoring country announced that it has reached a "framework" for a substantive trade agreement with its rival economy, which involves the other party's substantial increase in the purchase of agricultural products and assistance in the control of fentanyl precursor chemicals.
The initiating country and the rival economy reach a final agreement on a short video application transaction, which will be formally confirmed by the leaders of the two countries in a third country

Leaders of the sponsoring countries publicly stated that they would consider reducing tariffs on rival economies in exchange for controlling the export of fentanyl precursor chemicals, and for the first time clearly linked trade policy to anti-drug issues.

The first house of the sponsoring country's legislative body passed a resolution by a narrow majority to terminate the national emergency declaration based on the president's tariffs on a neighboring country. Several ruling party members defected, but the resolution was difficult to translate into law.
